analysis:
Documentation-only batch. changelog.d/gemma-tensor-parallel.md (head 1-7) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head 1125-1154) describe Gemma 4 tensor parallel across a two-Mac cluster. Ranks share per-token activations over an 'encrypted link' (A-001 plaintext-derived activations crossing machines). Both prefix tiers (memory and encrypted SSD) are retained for Gemma TP, and a restored prefix requires both Macs to hold it and survives a restart of both Macs. The per-rank memory budget (Gemma4TensorParallelRequestBudget) charges a 5.5 GiB conservative activation floor and prefix capture bytes. The prefix memory tier is uncharged and gives way before refusal (QwenStagePrefixCache.budget). DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_BATCH_LANES defaults to one lane.

Security-relevant questions for integration and source review, none evidenced as a regression here:
(1) The SSD tier for TP shards must keep T-041 controls: HMAC lookup tags, folding of the coordinator-authored cacheSalt into the tag and chain, the 30-minute TTL and the per-donation gate. The changelog line 6 'shared prompt prefix' wording must not imply cross-account reuse.
(2) The confidentiality and authentication of the inter-Mac cluster link, and the trust between peer ranks, are not covered by any listed TB. The threat model may need a cluster-link boundary if one is not already defined elsewhere.
(3) Memory accounting is unmeasured on a pair. An availability risk exists only if the 5.5 GiB floor is exceeded; this is documented as conservative.
(4) Logprobs are enabled for Gemma TP. Admission refusal for unsupported modes is unchanged (DistributedResidentExecutionProfile.refusal).

No code was supplied, so these controls cannot be verified from this batch.
